instruction:
Use ANSYS Workbench via the Command Line Interface (CLI) to complete a linear eigenvalue buckling analysis.

Physical problem:
A pin-ended straight column is subjected to axial compression.

Coordinate system and geometry:
- Use the global Cartesian coordinate system.
- Model the column as a line body with a beam cross-section.
- The column axis is along the global Y direction.
- The bottom end is located at Y = 0 mm.
- The top end is located at Y = 1000 mm.
- The rectangular beam section is:
  - Width = 10 mm
  - Height = 10 mm

Model parameters:
- Line body length: 1000 mm
- Section type: rectangular beam section
- Section size: 10 mm × 10 mm
- Material: Structural Steel with the following linear elastic properties:
  - Young's modulus E = 210000 MPa
  - Poisson's ratio ν = 0.3
- Use a consistent N-mm unit system.

Boundary conditions:
- Bottom end at Y = 0 mm:
  - Constrain UX = 0, UY = 0, and UZ = 0.
  - Leave all rotations free.
- Top end at Y = 1000 mm:
  - Constrain UX = 0 and UZ = 0.
  - Leave UY free.
  - Leave all rotations free.
- Apply an axial compressive reference load of 1 N at the top end in the negative global Y direction.

Analysis type:
- Linear eigenvalue buckling analysis.
- Extract the first buckling mode.

Save requirements:
- Use C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop as the working location.
- Save the Workbench project file as:
  C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\wb_buckling.wbpj
- Save the MAPDL-equivalent database file as:
  C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\wb_buckling.db
- Save the MAPDL-equivalent structural result file as:
  C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\wb_buckling.rst
